chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Bunan ibn Muhammad from Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) said:

I asked him about a man who cursed his wife and swore 'four testimonies by Allah', then hesitated/refused to give the fifth. He said: 'If he hesitates/refuses the fifth, then she is his wife and he is flogged. And if the wife hesitates/refuses that, when the oath is upon her, then upon her is the like of that.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal consequence if a husband stops swearing the fifth oath in the ritual of li'an?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) clarifies the procedural nuances of *li'an*, specifically addressing the scenario where the husband swears four oaths but hesitates on the fifth. It establishes that if he stops, the marriage bond remains intact and he receives the prescribed flogging, while the wife’s refusal to swear her counter-oath results in her incurring the same penalty, reflecting the juristic principle of symmetry in evidentiary oaths.
